target_customer: Consumers who want a hand-painted portrait or canvas from a photo, as gifts or decor
problem: Custom oil paintings from photos cost hundreds of dollars; Instapainting uses low cost artists, mostly in China, who paint over a printed photo to cut price and delivery time.
business_model: E-commerce marketplace taking margin on custom painting orders

founders.name: Chris Chen
founders.background_notes: Press release says the idea began when a friend asked him to build a site selling art reproductions sourced from China (accessnewswire). YC page lists only him.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web ordering flow and artist workflow management; the hard part was operations and quality control, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Competing painting shops could copy the print-and-paint-over model and sourcing; SEO was the main growth channel per a press release.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent acquired or copied it that sources show; the company remains small and active.

market_need_then: In February 2014 TechCrunch reported competitors charging $119 to $300 and up for a 12 inch oil painting from a photo versus about $53 at Instapainting, suggesting a price gap; no 2011 demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses instapainting.com; acquisition history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name that says what it does, but no press or community about the brand was found; a press release credits SEO for 60 percent of traffic.

outcome_analysis: Instapainting is an active, small e-commerce business that turns photos into paintings using outsourced artists. No funding amounts or exit were found, only a YC page statement that it is backed by Y Combinator and Start Fund. A press release credits SEO for most traffic, so it appears to have grown through organic search at modest scale; its current prices ($107 and up for oil) are higher than the 2014 launch prices.
notes: The YC page says it is backed by Y Combinator and Start Fund (SV Angel and Yuri Milner) but gives no amount or date, so no round is recorded; searches for funding found no database entry with amounts. Competitors named by TechCrunch (OilPaintingExpress, OilPaintings.com, myDavinci) come from a February 2014 article, three years after the Winter 2011 batch, so they are not listed as of founding. Public launch was February 2014 per TechCrunch. Revenue figures of about $400K per year and $32K per month are unreconciled.
